hypotheses.consequence: High-pressure hot caustic spray (sodium hydroxide) and sodium sulfide release; Na2S can generate H2S on contact with acid or water, creating toxic gas cloud; personnel chemical burns and H2S exposure; potential damage to nearby equipment.

hypotheses.consequence: Flammable and toxic liquid spray in pump area; pool fire if ignited; personnel exposure to methanol (toxic) and turpentine; potential vapour migration to nearby hot work on T-32 roof.
hypotheses.reason: High consequence (flammable/toxic release) and elevated likelihood: W-2 is planned maintenance on the seal; pump draws directly from T-33 containing the mixture; C06 is a library cause for this pump;

hypotheses.reason: High consequence (large unmitigated flammable release) and high likelihood: three 200 m³ atmospheric tanks with varying levels, organic layer floats on top, common vent/overflow headers, no level indication or high-level safeguard in plant record;

hypotheses.mechanism: The corroded 8-inch condensate line (L-CONDENSATE-8IN) on the T-32 roof fails (leak or rupture) before or during the planned replacement, spraying condensate (methanol, turpentine, organics) onto the hot work zone.

hypotheses.mechanism: Continuous venting of methanol, turpentine, and organics from the vent header (L-VENT-DISCHARGE) to atmosphere above the roofline encounters an ignition source (lightning strike, hot work, static discharge).

recommendations.action: Install a pressure relief valve on line L-T32-OVERFLOW set at design pressure, discharging to the process sewer.
recommendations.reason: No protection layers exist; a relief valve provides an independent engineered layer that directly relieves overpressure from downstream blockage, preferred over procedural controls.

recommendations.action: Upgrade STRIPPER-FEED-PUMP to a double mechanical seal with barrier fluid pressure monitoring and high-pressure alarm.
recommendations.reason: No layers exist; a double seal eliminates the single-point seal failure cause, preferred over leak detection which only mitigates after release.

recommendations.action: Install an interlock on valve W-2 that prevents opening when EVAPORATORS contain BLACK-LIQUOR, using a confirmed level/temperature signal.
recommendations.reason: The chain starts with operator error charging water into hot black liquor; an interlock removes the initiating cause at source, preventing the entire chain, preferred over mitigating later links.

recommendations.action: Add a low cooling water flow trip on UT-F-CW that automatically closes the steam supply valve to EVAPORATORS.
recommendations.reason: No layers exist; an independent trip on the utility loss stops heat input before pressure rises, preferred over a relief valve which only acts after overpressure.

recommendations.action: Install an independent low cooling water flow trip on UT-F-CW that isolates steam to EVAPORATORS and opens the vacuum system vent valve.
recommendations.reason: The chain shares loss of cooling water as a common cause for condenser and vacuum system overpressure; one engineered trip on UT-F-CW addresses both links, preferred over separate procedural responses.

recommendations.action: Install an independent pressure safety valve on S-SURFACE-CONDENSER venting to a safe location, sized for loss of cooling water (UT-F-CW) scenario.
recommendations.reason: No protection layers exist; this engineered layer directly mitigates the pressure build-up consequence from non-condensable accumulation when cooling water fails, preferred over procedural alarm as it acts automatically on the deviation.

recommendations.action: Install a locked-open valve and strainer on L-T33-VENT to prevent blockage from closed valve or solids deposition.
recommendations.reason: No layers exist; this removes the cause (internal blockage) by design, preferred over relief valve on unknown upstream tank or alarm requiring operator action, as it prevents the deviation entirely.

recommendations.action: Replace L-VENT-DISCHARGE with a fire-protected, full-bore vent line from VENT-HEADER to atmosphere with no valves, and install an independent fire-rated pressure safety valve on VENT-HEADER.
recommendations.reason: No layers exist for blockage or fire scenarios; this single action removes blockage cause (no valves, full bore) and adds engineered fire-rated overpressure protection on VENT-HEADER, covering all three deviations.

recommendations.action: Replace L-VENT-DISCHARGE with a fire-protected, full-bore vent line from VENT-HEADER to atmosphere with no valves, and install an independent fire-rated pressure safety valve on VENT-HEADER.
recommendations.reason: Same line and blockage cause as C1; this action serves both targets by eliminating blockage risk and providing overpressure protection for the no-flow scenario.

recommendations.action: Install a backup cooling water supply with automatic changeover to UT-F-CW for T-32 cooling to prevent temperature rise and flammable vapor generation on loss of primary cooling water.
recommendations.reason: No layers exist; this removes the cause (loss of cooling water) by design, preventing vapor cloud formation that hot work W-1 on LOC-F-T32-ROOF could ignite, preferred over ignition control or vapor mitigation as it addresses the root deviation.

recommendations.action: Install an independent high-level trip on T-31 with a dedicated level sensor that closes the T-31 inlet block valve(s) to stop inflow before liquid reaches the overflow line L-T31-OVERFLOW.
recommendations.reason: No protection layers exist. The scenario arises because high inflow continues while the overflow line is blocked; stopping inflow at the source removes the cause of overfill and subsequent vent blockage, which is preferable to adding relief on an atmospheric fixed-roof tank.

recommendations.action: Add an independent high-level trip on T-33 with a dedicated level sensor that closes the T-33 inlet valve(s) to halt inflow when the stripper feed pump (STRIPPER-FEED-PUMP) fails and the overflow header is blocked.
recommendations.reason: No protection layers exist. The pump failure combined with a blocked overflow header (L-T33-OVERFLOW) leaves T-33 with no relief path; an independent trip on T-33 level stops the continuing inflow before overpressure occurs, addressing the root cause rather than relying on the compromised overflow.

recommendations.action: Install an independent high-temperature trip on TK-WEAK-BLACK-LIQUOR with a dedicated temperature sensor that isolates steam tracing supply valves to the tank and activates the backup cooling water connection from UT-F-CW.
recommendations.reason: No protection layers exist. The primary deviation is uncontrolled temperature rise from cooling water loss or external heat; an independent trip that cuts heating sources and restores cooling directly counters the thermal decomposition mechanism generating H2S and flammable gases.

recommendations.action: Provide a fixed water deluge system on TK-WEAK-BLACK-LIQUOR with fire detection that automatically isolates steam tracing supply valves to the tank upon fire or excessive external heat detection.
recommendations.reason: No protection layers exist for the external heat cause (steam tracing, fire, hot work). A deluge system with automatic steam tracing isolation both removes the external heat source and cools the tank, preventing thermal decomposition and overpressure more reliably than procedural fire response.

recommendations.action: Add an independent high-temperature trip on T-33 with a dedicated temperature sensor that closes the steam heating supply valve to T-33 to stop excessive vapor generation before vent flow exceeds the capacity of L-T33-VENT.
recommendations.reason: No protection layers exist. The deviation is caused by steam heating raising tank temperature; an independent trip that isolates the steam heating source directly prevents the vapor surge, which is more effective than enlarging the vent or relying on operator response to high vent flow.
